analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 30th October
key_insights: EStoxx is -45bps at the open as the AI unwind resumes after the US close. The S&P finished near the day's highs (-30bps) while the Nasdaq lagged on disappointing hyperscaler earnings and capex guidance.

Post-close prints drove the move. Nasdaq futures are -1.9% after AMZN (-7%) missed on AWS growth and margins, and INTC (-23%) beat on the quarter but guided light on supply constraints. A SNDK beat offers little offset.
The desk puts the implied move for futures at about 80bps on index weights alone, so contagion risk for the broader AI complex is evident. NVDA is -1.6% after hours and the neoclouds are all lower.
Rotation was already under way on Thursday. Value outperformed Growth by 2.7% and Consumer Staples (+1.6%) beat the SOX (-1.4%). MDLZ is +7.6% after hours on results.
Asia is lower in pockets in sympathy with the US. Taiex is -2.5% and Japan is sharply lower. The Hang Seng (+1.4%) is the regional outlier.

The BoJ held at 8-1 with a modestly hawkish message that keeps a December hike in play. It said the inflation trend has reached its 2% target, and the yen is firmer near 157.60/USD within a broad dollar sell-off. CHF leads the G10 board on haven demand.

The BoJ raised its FY2027 core CPI forecast to 2.6% versus UBS's 2.5%, put more weight on wage-price dynamics and inflation-expectation risks, left the proposed food-tax cut out of its forecasts, and accelerated ETF disposals from January 2027. FY2027 growth is slightly soft at 0.7%.

The 10yr extends Thursday's rally to 4.92% (-2bps). WTI briefly broke $105 and settled near $103 after Iran signalled no change in its peace deal terms on receipt of Vance's letter. The desk says the energy risk premium stays embedded into the weekend, and that a few dollars either way in crude has had muted impact on equities for now.

The desk's open question into the weekend is whether the AI complex sees an orderly rotation into defensives and value, or a broader de-gross across momentum and equities in general. Lower yields are providing some support.

Thursday's European cash flows were balanced (50/50) with elevated turnover during earnings season. Banks were the busiest sector at 17% of turnover and finished better to buy on strong demand for Spanish names.
